nodes.name: Architecture
nodes.description: The art and technique of designing and constructing buildings and spaces.

nodes.name: Architectural Styles
nodes.description: Historical and regional styles of building design.

nodes.name: Romanesque
nodes.description: Medieval European style of round arches and massive walls.

nodes.name: Gothic
nodes.description: Medieval style of pointed arches, rib vaults, and flying buttresses.

nodes.name: Renaissance Architecture
nodes.description: 15th-16th century revival of classical orders and proportion.

nodes.name: Baroque Architecture
nodes.description: 17th-century dramatic architecture of curves, light, and grandeur.

nodes.name: Neoclassical Architecture
nodes.description: 18th-19th century revival of Greek and Roman forms.

nodes.name: Beaux-Arts
nodes.description: Academic 19th-century style of monumentality and classical ornament.

nodes.name: Art Nouveau Architecture
nodes.description: Organic, curvilinear architecture of the late 19th century.

nodes.name: Art Deco Architecture
nodes.description: 1920s-30s style of geometric ornament and streamlined form.

nodes.name: Modernist Architecture
nodes.description: 20th-century architecture of functionalism, minimalism, and new materials.

nodes.name: International Style
nodes.description: Modernist style of glass, steel, and volume without ornament.

nodes.name: Brutalism
nodes.description: Mid-20th-century style of raw exposed concrete and massive form.

nodes.name: Postmodern Architecture
nodes.description: Late 20th-century style reintroducing ornament, color, and historical reference.

nodes.name: Deconstructivism
nodes.description: Late 20th-century architecture of fragmented, non-rectilinear form.

nodes.name: High-Tech Architecture
nodes.description: Late 20th-century style expressing structure and technology.

nodes.name: Organic Architecture
nodes.description: Architecture harmonizing building, site, and nature.

nodes.name: Critical Regionalism
nodes.description: Architecture responding to local context against placeless modernism.

nodes.name: Islamic Architecture
nodes.description: Architecture of the Islamic world featuring arches, domes, and geometric ornament.

nodes.name: Chinese Architecture
nodes.description: Chinese building tradition of timber frames, dougong brackets, and courtyards.

nodes.name: Japanese Architecture
nodes.description: Japanese building tradition of timber, tatami, and harmony with nature.

nodes.name: Indian Architecture
nodes.description: Architecture of the Indian subcontinent spanning stupas, temples, and Mughal monuments.

nodes.name: Byzantine Architecture
nodes.description: Eastern Roman architecture of domes and mosaics.

nodes.name: Mesoamerican Architecture
nodes.description: Pyramids and temples of Maya, Aztec, and other Mesoamerican cultures.

nodes.name: Building Types
nodes.description: Categories of buildings by function.

nodes.name: Religious Architecture
nodes.description: Buildings for worship, from temples to cathedrals and mosques.

nodes.name: Residential Architecture
nodes.description: Design of homes and dwellings.

nodes.name: Civic Architecture
nodes.description: Public buildings such as libraries, museums, and government halls.

nodes.name: Commercial Architecture
nodes.description: Buildings for commerce, from shops to office towers.

nodes.name: Industrial Architecture
nodes.description: Buildings for manufacturing and infrastructure.

nodes.name: Vernacular Architecture
nodes.description: Traditional building using local materials and techniques.

nodes.name: Landscape Architecture
nodes.description: Design of outdoor spaces, gardens, and public landscapes.

nodes.name: Urban Design
nodes.description: The design of cities, districts, and public space.

nodes.name: Sustainable Architecture
nodes.description: Building design minimizing environmental impact and resource use.
